[Textbook answer-key error: the printed MCQ key marks (B) \(\pm 3\); the coincident-lines condition gives \(h = \pm 4\), so the correct option is (C) (our marked answer).]

Coincident lines require \(h^2 = ab\), where \(a = 4,\ b = 1\) and \(h\) is the coefficient (\(2h\)-form gives the same relation on \(h^2\)). So \(h^2 = 4 \cdot 1 \cdot 4 = 16\), giving \(h = \pm 4\). — option C
Lines through the origin are perpendicular when \(a + b = 0\). For \(kx^2 - 3xy + 6y^2 = 0\), \(a = k,\ b = 6\), so \(k + 6 = 0\), giving \(k = -6\). — option B

Putting \(y = mx\) (or dividing by \(x^2\) and setting \(m = y/x\)) in \(2x^2 + 3xy - 9y^2 = 0\) gives the auxiliary equation \(bm^2 + 2hm + a = 0\): \(-9m^2 + 3m + 2 = 0\), i.e. \(9m^2 - 3m - 2 = 0\). — option B

With slopes \(m_1 = \tan\alpha,\ m_2 = \tan\beta\), we have \(m_1 + m_2 = -\frac{2h}{b}\) and \(m_1 m_2 = \frac{a}{b}\). Thus \(\tan(\alpha+\beta) = \frac{m_1 + m_2}{1 - m_1 m_2} = \frac{-2h/b}{1 - a/b} = \frac{-2h}{b - a} = \frac{2h}{a - b}\). — option D

Here \(A = \frac{1}{a},\ 2H = \frac{2}{h}\Rightarrow H = \frac{1}{h},\ B = \frac{1}{b}\). One slope twice the other requires \(8H^2 = 9AB\): \(\frac{8}{h^2} = \frac{9}{ab}\), so \(ab : h^2 = 9 : 8\). — option D

The pair perpendicular to \(ax^2 + 2hxy + by^2 = 0\) is \(bx^2 - 2hxy + ay^2 = 0\). For \(3x^2 + 4xy - 5y^2 = 0\) (\(a=3,\ 2h=4,\ b=-5\)) this gives \(-5x^2 - 4xy + 3y^2 = 0\), i.e. \(5x^2 + 4xy - 3y^2 = 0\). — option A

With \(\theta = \frac{\pi}{4}\), \(\tan\theta = 1 = \left|\frac{2\sqrt{h^2 - ab}}{a + b}\right|\), so \((a+b)^2 = 4(h^2 - ab)\). Expanding: \(a^2 + 2ab + b^2 = 4h^2 - 4ab\), giving \(4h^2 = a^2 + 6ab + b^2\). — option B

Write as \(3x^2 - 8xy + qy^2 + 2x + 14y + (p-1) = 0\), so \(a=3,\ b=q,\ h=-4,\ g=1,\ f=7,\ c=p-1\). Perpendicular lines need \(a+b=0\Rightarrow q=-3\). The pair condition \(abc + 2fgh - af^2 - bg^2 - ch^2 = 0\) gives \(-25(p-1) - 200 = 0\Rightarrow p = -7\). So \(p=-7,\ q=-3\). — option B

The pair \(x^2 + 4xy + y^2 = 0\) gives slopes \(m = -2 \pm \sqrt{3}\). Finding where each meets the base line \(x - y - 4 = 0\) and taking the triangle with the origin yields area \(= \frac{n^2 \sqrt{h^2 - ab}}{|am^2 - 2hlm + bl^2|}\)-type value \(= \frac{8}{\sqrt{3}}\) sq. units (verified numerically). — option B
The coordinate axes are \(x = 0\) (Y-axis) and \(y = 0\) (X-axis); their combined equation is the product \(x \cdot y = 0\), i.e. \(xy = 0\). — option C

[Textbook answer-key error: the printed MCQ key marks (C) \(2:3\); coincident lines have equal slopes, so the ratio is \(1:1\) — the correct option is (D) (our marked answer).]

\(h^2 = ab\) is the condition for coincident lines, so the two slopes are equal and their ratio is \(1 : 1\). — option D

Let \(m_1 = 5m_2\). Then \(\frac{(m_1+m_2)^2}{m_1 m_2} = \frac{(6m_2)^2}{5m_2^2} = \frac{36}{5}\), and \(\frac{(m_1+m_2)^2}{m_1 m_2} = \frac{(-2h/b)^2}{a/b} = \frac{4h^2}{ab}\). So \(\frac{4h^2}{ab} = \frac{36}{5}\Rightarrow 20h^2 = 36ab\Rightarrow 5h^2 = 9ab\). — option D

Put \(u = x - 2y\): \(u^2 + ku = 0\Rightarrow u(u+k)=0\), giving parallel lines \(x - 2y = 0\) and \(x - 2y + k = 0\). Their distance is \(\frac{|k|}{\sqrt{1^2 + 2^2}} = \frac{|k|}{\sqrt{5}} = 3\), so \(|k| = 3\sqrt{5}\), i.e. \(k = \pm 3\sqrt{5}\). — option D
